summary: Hermann Camillo Kellner worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1865–1868) and served as Gymnasialprofessor at Königliches Gymnasium Zwickau (~1874–1904).

Hermann Collitz was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Johanneum Lüneburg, Göttingen under August Fick, Berlin, and Halle-Wittenberg. He taught at Bryn Mawr College (1885–1907) and held the chair of Germanic philology at Johns Hopkins University (1907–1928).
Hermann Ernst Grassmann studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1880). He later served as professor of mathematics at the University of Giessen (~1893–1922).

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, Hermann Goetz studied at Munich and under Jean Philippe Vogel. He held posts at the Baroda Museum (1939–1953), National Gallery of Modern Art (~1953–1955), and Heidelberg University (1961–1976).
Hermann Güntert was a scholar in linguistics, Indology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1921–1926) and Heidelberg University (~1926–1945).

Hermann Günther Grassmann was an Indologist, linguist, and mathematician. He studied at Marienstiftsgymnasium and Humboldt University of Berlin under Friedrich Schleiermacher. He taught at Gewerbeschule Berlin, Friedrich-Wilhelms-Gymnasium, and as professor at Marienstiftsgymnasium (1852–1877).

Hermann Hirt worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the University of Freiburg and Leipzig University, where he was a Privatdozent (1891–1912). He was later professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at the University of Giessen (1912–1936).

Hermann Hunger is a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Vienna, Münster, and Heidelberg. His career included posts at the German Archaeological Institute (~1970–1973), University of Chicago (~1973–1978), and University of Vienna (~1978–2007).

Indologist and linguist Hermann Jacobi studied at Bonn under Johann Gildemeister, Humboldt University under Albrecht Weber, and Calcutta. He served as professor at Münster (1876–1885), Kiel (1885), and Bonn (1889–1922), with posts at Cologne and Munich.

Indologist and historian Hermann Kulke studied at Madras, Freiburg under Hermann Goetz, and Heidelberg. He held posts at Heidelberg University (1967–1988) and served as Chair of Asian History at Kiel University (1988–2003).

Hermann Oldenberg worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Göttingen and Humboldt University of Berlin, where he became professor in 1878. He later served as professor at Kiel University (1889, 1898) and Göttingen (1908).

Linguist and Indologist Hermann Osthoff studied at Berlin, Tübingen, Bonn under Hermann Usener, and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He served as a Privatdozent at Leipzig (~1875–1877) and became Ordinarius at Heidelberg University in 1877.

Hermann Sauppe was a classical scholar and linguist. He earned his doctorate at Leipzig University under Gottfried Hermann. He later held positions at the University of Zurich (1833, 1838) and served as professor at the University of Göttingen from 1855.

Hermann Usener was a scholar of religious studies, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at Heidelberg, Munich, Göttingen, and Bonn. He held academic posts at the University of Bern (~1861–1863), University of Greifswald (~1863–1866), and University of Bonn (~1866–1902).

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel was a linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott and Berlin under August Boeckh and Franz Bopp. He taught at Gymnasium Schneidemühl (1858) and held the chair of comparative philology at Berlin (1872).
Hermann von Schlagintweit worked in history, archaeology, and other fields. He studied at the University of Munich (~1846–1849) and held a teaching post at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1851–1854).

Heymann Steinthal was a scholar in linguistics and philosophy who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under August Boeckh. He held academic posts at Frederick William / Humboldt University (~1850–1899) and the Hochschule für die Wissenschaft des Judentums (~1872–1899).
Hideaki Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral studies at Taisho University (~1980–1986) and was attested there as a researcher in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin M. Nagao and Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hideki Kiyoshima works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Delhi and was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.
